title: Server-state cache separated from UI state, stale-while-revalidate by default
context: application-spa-REQ-013 requires a client cache discipline. Whether client state is one store or two regimes is a whole-project decision; mixing regimes per feature produces stale lists, flicker, and phantom optimistic state.
decision: Server state lives in a keyed query cache with stale-while-revalidate reads and explicit invalidation on writes. UI state (selection, open panels, form drafts) lives in local component or page state and never enters the server-state cache. Optimistic updates are opt-in per mutation and roll back visibly on failure. Cache keys derive from canonical resource URLs.
consequences: Data freshness has one policy to verify. Screens read query status instead of hand-rolling loading flags, which is what makes the application-spa-REQ-010 state quartet cheap. The discipline forbids stuffing view state into the cache even when convenient.

alternativesConsidered.name: Single global store for everything
alternativesConsidered.summary: One store holding server data and view state.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Couples wire lifecycles to view lifecycles; invalidation becomes manual and error-prone.

alternativesConsidered.name: Fetch-per-render, no cache
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Fails the performance budget and produces loading flicker on every navigation.
